researched.name: Msafe Equipments Ltd
researched.reason: Q2 FY27 revenue Rs 40.38 cr (+53.59% YoY) and PAT Rs 8.49 cr (+55.42%) at a 38.65% EBITDA margin, with H1 FY27 revenue of Rs 72.17 cr already 69.7% of the whole of FY26 and H1 PAT of Rs 15.76 cr 70.3% of FY26's Rs 22.42 cr. Published at MEDIUM confidence. What made it publishable rather than another results pop: the profit growth is NOT a tax or incentive artefact - PBT grew 52.9% in the quarter and 49.8% in the half, in line with PAT, and material cost grew only 22.9% against revenue up 53.6%, so the operating line carries it. The mechanism is readable and physical: the rental share of revenue went 46% -> 52%, MS rental revenue grew 7x YoY in Q1 FY27 on capacity added through temporary rented premises, and the company states rental yields of 60-66% a year on aluminium and 32-38% on MS. Management's FY27 target is in two filed documents ('approximately 50% revenue growth', 2-Nov-2026 deck; 'We will definitely do Rs 150 crores, but we will really try to achieve Rs 175 crores', Q1 FY27 call transcript, 13-Aug-2026), and the arithmetic reconciles exactly to BSE's own header - TTM PAT Rs 27.68 cr on 2.04 cr shares gives EPS 13.57 and PE 20.93, which is what BSE prints. Forward 17.4x FY27E, against the only genuine listed rental comparable, Sanghvi Movers at 17.31x. The card carries three warnings of equal weight: Rs 30.46 cr appeared in 'other non-current assets' during the half with no explanation anywhere in the deck (27% of net worth); the aluminium formwork line has already slipped once, from 'the end of June' 2026 to December 2026; and the FY26 annual report was not among the extracted documents, so related-party transactions, promoter remuneration and auditor remarks are stated as UNANSWERED rather than clean. The call price also follows a 19.1% day on 4.4x median volume, which this page's own study says is an alarm bell, not evidence, and the card says so.

researched.name: Sunita Tools Ltd
researched.reason: The day's highest-scoring candidate (9.0) and the one that looked best from the headline: a Reg-30 Award-of-Order filed 02-Nov-2026 at 14:53 for M1 shell forging from a Central Public Sector Undertaking, plus a press release announcing OEM qualification for forging empty shells for an Ordnance Factory of the Government of India. Declined after reading the filings, for reasons that only reading produced. THE ORDER HAS NO VALUE: the Reg-30 annexure answers 'Broad consideration or size of the order(s)/contract(s)' with 'Not disclosed due to confidentiality', names the awarding entity as 'Not disclosed due to confidentiality', and gives the execution period as 'As soon as possible.' The only quantity is 6,000 sets. The 2026-09-22 order study requires an order to be sized against a trailing year of sales, and that cannot be done here at all. THE FLAGSHIP AGREEMENT IS ALSO UNQUANTIFIED: four press releases in 240 days (09-Mar, 10-Jun, 20-Jul, 17-Sep 2026) report tranches of advance payment against an 'Interim Sales Agreement' for NATO-spec 155mm M107 empty shells; the 17-Sep release was read in full and states no value, no quantity and no counterparty. The FY26 annual report is more cautious than the press releases: it calls the programme 'a capability-development and commercialisation initiative' whose 'commercial production and supply remain subject to applicable regulatory approvals, licences, prototype/product qualification, customer approvals and other contractual conditions', and the June-2026 investor presentation says 'DPIIT license awaited'. AND THE BALANCE SHEET DOES NOT SHOW THE ADVANCES: 'Advance from customers' is NIL at 31-Mar-2026 in BOTH the standalone and consolidated Other Current Liabilities notes, against Rs 3.44 lakh at 31-Mar-2025 - the documents read do not reconcile that with the 09-Mar-2026 advance-payment press release, and it is recorded here as an unexplained gap, not as proof of anything. The valuation leaves no room for any of this to go wrong: BSE's header prints PE 107.05 on EPS 10.28, market cap Rs 691 cr on FY26 revenue of Rs 46.44 cr and PAT of Rs 6.51 cr. FY26 export sales were Rs 0.24 LAKH - twenty-four thousand rupees - so the 56.8% FY26 revenue growth is the legacy mould-base and CNC business, not shells. Management's filed projection is FY27 Rs 161 cr, FY28 Rs 309 cr, FY29 Rs 636 cr of sales against FY26's Rs 46 cr, marked '*Subject to various conditions'. Promoter holding fell from 67.18% (Sep-2025) to 62.75% (Sep-2026). The secretarial auditor records a four-day delay in reporting the interim sales agreement under Reg 30, an LODR related-party format deviation settled by paying an SOP fine, and a PAS-3 filed with an uncertified list of allottees on a warrant conversion. A genuinely interesting defence story - and one where every number that would make it an idea is withheld by the company.

researched.name: Jay Bharat Maruti Ltd
researched.reason: Rose 13.3% on 3.9x median volume on its Q2 FY27 results and looked, from BSE's results feed, like a clean beat: revenue Rs 823.42 cr (+41.3% YoY) and PAT Rs 31.12 cr (+72.6%) at PE 9.45, PB 2.62, ROE 27.74 and a market cap of Rs 1,409 cr. The company's own presentation, filed at 19:48 on 02-Nov-2026, takes the beat apart. The PAT footnote reads, verbatim: 'CY Q2 PAT is higher due to lower tax rate on adoption of new tax regime, revised tax rate is 25.17% from 34.94%.' PBT - the line the tax change cannot touch - grew 46.8% in the quarter but only 9.46% in the half (Rs 69.97 cr vs Rs 63.92 cr) against H1 revenue growth of 27.62%. The EBITDA margin FELL, 10.70% to 9.65% in the quarter and 11.25% to 9.83% in the half, with material cost up 193 bps to 75.49% of income, which the deck attributes to 'adverse commodity prices in context of West Asia Conflict'. And the deck discloses that EBITDA itself is substantially a subsidy: 'Q2 CY EBIDTA percentage is lower due to less Incentive eligibility as compared to Q1 PY (29.80 Cr vs. 34.26 Cr)' - Rs 29.80 cr of state incentive inside Q2 EBITDA of Rs 79.96 cr, 37.3% of it, with the positive-factors list separately naming a 'State Incentive of previous FY from Govt. of Gujarat'. Strip incentives and Q2 EBITDA is about Rs 50.2 cr on Rs 828.68 cr of income, a 6.1% margin. The volume growth is real - sheet-metal turnover up 42% YoY on higher Maruti Suzuki volumes and new plants - but the earnings the market re-rated today are a tax-rate change plus a state incentive, and the company gives no revenue or margin guidance to model against. Declined: the trigger does not survive its own document.

THE PYTHON-INTERPRETER TRAP RECURRED FOR A FOURTH RUN, AND THIS TIME IT BIT BEFORE IT WAS CAUGHT. Step 0 of the routine prompt says `pip install --quiet pymupdf`, but on this VM `pip` is python3.13's while the interpreter that runs the builders is /usr/local/bin/python3 = Python 3.11.18. The install reported 'Requirement already satisfied' into /usr/local/lib/python3.13/site-packages and `import fitz` still failed. The consequence this run: spot.py and govt.py ran before the trap was spotted (no harm - they do not use fitz), but MINSTEEL.PY CRASHED OUTRIGHT with ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'fitz' on its first invocation and had to be re-run. Fixed with `python3 -m pip install pymupdf xlrd`, after which fitz and xlrd both imported and minsteel.py, india_spot.py, scan.py and dossier.py all ran clean. SUGGESTED FIX, now four runs old: change step 0 of the routine prompt from `pip install --quiet pymupdf` to `python3 -m pip install --quiet pymupdf xlrd`.
